JUDGMENT The petitioner has filed the petition under Section 12 of Protection of Woman from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 against the respondents for seeking various relief under the Act.

1 this Court. As a result, this Court received the complete case file and proceeded with the matter, as per the order dated 15.09.2022.
3. The case of the petitioner in brief is as under:
a. The petitioner is the legally wedded wife of respondent No. 1, with their marriage solemnized on April 23, 2012, at Sri Gangadhareshwara Kalyan Mantap, Kunigal,
Tumkur District, according to Hindu rites and customs. They have one male child from their marriage. At the time of the marriage, the respondents demanded and received dowry in the form of cash amounting to 50,000 and gold jewelry, including a 10-gram ring and a 25-gram neck chain. The petitioner's parents fulfilled these demands. The entire wedding expenses, amounting to 6 lakhs, were borne by the petitioner's parents as desired by the respondents. 
Crl.Misc.No.163/2022 JUDGMENT b. After the marriage, the petitioner moved into the matrimonial home with respondent No. 1 and his family, including respondents No. 2 and 3 (father and mother-in-law), respondent No. 4 (brother-in-law),
respondent No. 5 (sister-in- law), and respondent No. 6 (sister-in-law). From the very beginning, there was no cordial relationship between the petitioner and respondent No. 1. Immediately after entering the matrimonial home, the respondents began to harass and torture the petitioner for additional dowry. As a practicing advocate in Bengaluru, the petitioner faced threats from respondent No. 5 to stop her legal practice and not to cohabit with respondent No. 1. Respondent No. 5 threatened that if the petitioner raised her voice, she would be killed by burning, and her parents would face the same fate if they supported her. Respondent No. 1 ignored the petitioner's complaints about respondent No. 5 and instructed her to comply with their demands. 
c. Further, the petitioner stated that respondent No.1 would often initiate unnecessary quarrels with her, during which respondent No.1 and the other respondents would Crl.Misc.No.163/2022 JUDGMENT assault her with whatever they had at hand, causing injuries. The respondents have been continuously harassing the petitioner, demanding that she bring dowry from her parents or secure her share of property from her mother's estate. The petitioner informed them that her mother had already incurred significant expenses for her marriage and had no money to give to the respondents. Upon hearing this, respondents No.1 and 5 assaulted the petitioner, causing severe bodily injuries. The pain from the assault was unbearable, and the petitioner screamed for help. 
Hearing her cries, the neighbors informed the Channammanakere police. The police took all the respondents into custody and warned them not to engage in any further acts of harassment against the petitioner. Subsequently, respondent No.1 demanded that the petitioner stop practicing as an advocate, while also using her to handle his own legal cases. 
d. The petitioner further stated that respondent No.1 would physically assault and mentally torture her, often suspecting her over trivial matters. She was made to work all Crl.Misc.No.163/2022 JUDGMENT day without being provided proper food, while respondent No.5, who did not Smt Varalakshmi M N vs Sri Ashoka T on 21 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134505335/
2 contribute to household work, would order the petitioner to do everything. Respondent No.5 also instigated quarrels between respondent No.1 and the petitioner. Respondent No.1 never treated the petitioner as his wife, continually assaulting and harassing her both physically and mentally, and failed to provide for her basic needs. Respondent No.1, along with the other respondents, harassed the petitioner without any cause, demanding that she bring money from her mother, knowing that her father had passed away long ago. Despite being fully aware of the petitioner's background and her widow mother's situation, the respondents unjustly pressured her to bring money. 
e. The petitioner further stated that the harassment by the respondents increased day by day,
becoming unbearable. Unable to endure the abuse any longer, she approached the Thyagarajanagar Women's Police Station to report the harassment and torture. In response, respondents No.1 and 2 promised before the police authorities that they Crl.Misc.No.163/2022 JUDGMENT would stop harassing her and gave this assurance in writing. Respondent No.5, however, continued to speak ill of the petitioner to respondent No.1, preventing him from cohabiting with her. The petitioner informed her family about respondent No.5's actions, and during a panchayat meeting, respondent No.1 was advised to lead a happy marital life with the petitioner. However, he continued to listen to respondent No.5 and neglected his duty to maintain the petitioner. 
f. The petitioner was three months pregnant when she informed respondent No.1 of her condition. 
However, he was not pleased, and under the influence of respondents No.2 to 6, respondent No.1 asked the petitioner to abort the pregnancy, stating that she did not belong to his family. He also informed her that whatever income he earned would be given to respondent No.5 and her children. 
The respondents made it a daily routine to assault and harass the petitioner, threatening her to abort the pregnancy. Fearing for her safety, the petitioner left the respondents' house and moved in with her mother. While staying at her mother's house, her mother Crl.Misc.No.163/2022 JUDGMENT took care of her daily needs. During this time, respondent No.1 neither visited the petitioner nor provided any financial support for her maintenance. The petitioner gave birth to a male child on 03.06.2014, with all the medical expenses covered by her mother. Although the birth of the child was communicated to respondent No.1, instead of visiting, he demanded Rs.50,000 from the petitioner to see the child. Left with no other option, the petitioner paid the amount using her ATM card. Despite this, the petitioner and the child stayed at her mother's house for nearly nine months, during which respondent No.1 never visited or saw them. 
g. After nine months, the petitioner returned to the matrimonial home with her child. At that time,
respondent No.1 began to claim that the child was not his and accused the petitioner of infidelity. 
This caused the petitioner severe emotional hardship and depression. She had endured all the harassment in the hope that respondent No.1 would change after the birth of their child, but his attitude remained unchanged. The gold ornaments given to the petitioner by her Crl.Misc.No.163/2022 JUDGMENT mother at the time of marriage were taken by respondent No.1 and sold to fund his extravagant lifestyle. When the petitioner questioned this, respondent No.1 informed her that he had used the money to purchase land bearing Sy.No.114, measuring 1 acre, at K. Choodahalli village in his father's name. Respondent No.1 had obtained a General Power of Attorney (GPA) from his father for the land, formed a layout of sites, sold most of the plots to buyers, and retained only two. The sale proceeds were divided among the respondents, with no Smt Varalakshmi M N vs Sri Ashoka T on 21 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134505335/
3 amount given to the petitioner or her child. The petitioner made several efforts to persuade respondent No.1 to change his behavior, but he remained unchanged. Respondent No.1 again assaulted the petitioner, this time in front of their housemaid, and this pattern of abuse continued. 
Despite enduring repeated assaults, the petitioner tolerated the abuse for the sake of her family and child. 
h. Respondent No.1 never engaged in a physical relationship with the petitioner. Whenever the petitioner attempted to get close, he would avoid her and suggest that Crl.Misc.No.163/2022 JUDGMENT she cohabit with someone else. When the petitioner was two and a half months pregnant, respondent No.1 gave her tablets that caused her to lose the pregnancy. Although respondent No.1 would occasionally engage in sexual relations with the petitioner, he repeatedly caused her to abort any pregnancies. 
i. The petitioner further stated that respondent No.1, who had no interest in her, conspired to murder her by hiring criminal elements, using his financial power to cover up the crime. Upon learning about this conspiracy, the petitioner felt threatened. Respondent No.1 then renewed his demands for dowry from her parents or urged her to sell property and bring her share of the proceeds. The petitioner explained that her mother was unable to meet these demands, leading to heated arguments between them. During one such argument, respondent No.1 assaulted the petitioner, stating that if he had married someone else, he would have received more dowry. He admitted to marrying the petitioner only because she was an only daughter, capable of providing the dowry he demanded. When the petitioner refused to comply, respondent Crl.Misc.No.163/2022 JUDGMENT No.1 assaulted her with a club, causing bodily injuries for which she sought treatment at a government hospital in Udupi. 
j. Unable to bear the abuse any longer, the petitioner lodged a complaint against the respondents at the Udupi Women's Police Station on 15.11.2018. However, the police did not register the case against respondent No.1, as he was serving as the Civil Judge, 4th Addl. JMFC, Udupi. Using his influence, he avoided having the case registered. Instead, the police sent both parties for counselling, which failed due to respondent No.1's actions. After the petitioner lodged the complaint, respondent No.1 voluntarily deserted her and their child, moving back to his parents'
home in Bengaluru. The petitioner and her child remained in Udupi. 
k. When the petitioner realized that respondent No.1 had abandoned them, she tried contacting him,
but was unsuccessful. Unable to support herself and the child, the petitioner was forced to move to Bengaluru, causing her child to miss school. With the help of friends, relatives, and by Crl.Misc.No.163/2022 JUDGMENT taking out a personal loan, she rented a house, where she and her child currently reside. The petitioner's mother, a widow with no source of income, is barely managing to sustain herself. If the petitioner and her child were to stay with her mother, they would become an additional burden. 
l. Respondent No.1, along with a relative, came to the JP Nagar residence and assaulted the petitioner. The petitioner lodged a police complaint, which was registered as an NCR. The petitioner is facing significant difficulties in meeting her daily needs, and her elderly mother has no source of Smt Varalakshmi M N vs Sri Ashoka T on 21 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134505335/
4 income. Due to financial constraints, she has been unable to admit her child in school, and the child is currently staying with her and not attending school. Although this situation was brought to respondent No.1's attention, he refused to provide any financial support for the child's education. 
m. The petitioner has been forced to take out personal loans to cover her daily expenses and is struggling to pay rent. She further stated that all respondent No.1's actions have violated her dignity,
subjecting her to systematic verbal and Crl.Misc.No.163/2022 JUDGMENT emotional abuse, which has continued daily. The petitioner is no longer able to endure the ongoing torture. Respondent No.1 is currently appointed as a Civil Judge (OOD Leave Reserve) at the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru, earning a salary of Rs.68,703, which has since increased to Rs.1,00,000 per month. As a Group-A officer, his salary increments annually, and he also receives arrears exceeding Rs.1,00,000 each year. Additionally, respondent No.1 has Rs.35 lakhs deposited in his bank account,
as declared to the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka during his appointment. He also owns agricultural properties in his native place, from which he earns Rs.50,000 per month, as well as movable assets, including a Wagon R car and a two-wheeler. Overall, respondent No.1 has a monthly income of Rs.2,50,000. Despite this, respondent No.1 has completely neglected the petitioner and their minor child without justification, and he continues to refuse to provide any financial support or maintenance for them. The petitioner is finding it extremely difficult to meet her and her child's daily needs. She is currently living with her parents and facing severe financial Crl.Misc.No.163/2022 JUDGMENT hardship, with no source of income to lead a normal life. With these averments, petitioner prayed that the petition be allowed.

He asserts that there is no cause of action to file the petition, and that the Crl.Misc.No.163/2022 JUDGMENT cause of action shown by the petitioner is fabricated in order to create a false case and mislead the court to obtain relief.

The respondent further submits that the petitioner only lived for one day with Respondents No. 2 and 3 when she was brought to their home. During this time, she frequently quarrelled with the Smt Varalakshmi M N vs Sri Ashoka T on 21 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134505335/

6. The statement of objections of respondent No.2 to 6 is as follows:
Respondents No. 2 to 6 submit that the petitioner has suppressed material facts and fabricated a false case against them. The respondents were present at the petitioner and Respondent No. 1's wedding, but neither the petitioner nor Respondent No. 1 ever lived with Respondents No. 2 to 6. The petitioner has never contacted Respondents No. 2 to 6 by phone, nor have the respondents been in touch with her. 
Respondents No. 2 and 3 reside in a village, Respondents No. 4 and 5 live separately,
and Respondent No. 6 is living with her husband. The petitioner has named them as parties solely to pressure Respondent No. 1. With these contentions, prayed to reject the petition.

It was further argued that Respondent No. 1 failed to provide any financial support for the petitioner and their child, which constitutes economic abuse. At the very outset, it is pertinent to mention that complainant in order to be entitled to the relief under the Domestic Violence Act, 2005 is required to establish, that firstly there is a domestic relationship as defined under Section 2(f) of the abovesaid Act between complainant and respondents and thereafter it is also required to be established Crl.Misc.No.163/2022 JUDGMENT that she has been a victim of domestic violence as defined under Section 3 of the said Act. Domestic relationship has been defined under the Act in Section 2(f) as under:
(f)"domestic relationship" means a relationship between two persons who live or have, at any point of time, lived together in a shared household, when they are related by consanguinity, marriage, or through a relationship in the nature of marriage, adoption or are family members living together as a joint family.
18. It is observed that the fact of the marriage between the petitioner and Respondent No. 1 is not disputed by either party. This is further substantiated through documentary evidence marked as Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2, which include the marriage card and photographs of the marriage. It is also undisputed that Master Dhanith.A was born from this union. Therefore, the domestic relationship between the petitioner and Respondent No.1 is established. As for the domestic relationship between the petitioner and the other respondents, the petitioner has asserted that such a relationship exists. However, the other respondents have denied this claim, arguing that after the petitioner and Respondent No. 1 moved Crl.Misc.No.163/2022 JUDGMENT out of the matrimonial home and were disowned, no domestic relationship remains.

313 read with Section 149 of the Indian Penal Code. After completing the investigation, the police submitted a charge sheet against the respondents before the Hon'ble 2nd Additional Civil Judge and JMFC Court, Udupi, as evidenced by Ex.P.3, P.4, P.14, and P.27.

As it stands, the criminal case is still pending and under consideration concerning the allegations of dowry demands and cruelty.
